name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "The Glu-to-Lys charge reversal at residue 1021 adds a positive charge on the helix (1008-1031) that increases electrostatic attraction to the negatively charged PIP2 head groups of the membrane, so p110\u03b4 associates with membranes more strongly and produces more PIP3 (the reported gain-of-function phenotype).", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E2", "E7", "E13", "E14", "E16", "E17", "E18", "E20"], "would_refute": "Residue 1021 lies more than about 10 \u00c5 from the membrane-facing surface and from the ATP and inhibitor sites in the experimental structures, and the electrostatic surface potential or membrane-docking simulations show no measurable change in membrane binding for E1021K versus wild type.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "E2 explicitly describes the variant as causing enhanced membrane association and kinase activity, which this mechanism directly explains. E7 and E7/E9 place 1021 in the catalytic domain, and E17/E18 show the residue is observed across 20 structures, including inhibitor-bound ones, so it is near the active site. There is no residue-level membrane or lipid data for E1021K (G1, G2), so this rank rests on the UniProt description alone and not on any measurement of this substitution."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "E1021 sits on a surface contact with the regulatory p85 subunit (or its inhibitory SH2 region) that normally restrains p110\u03b4; the Glu-to-Lys change disrupts that electrostatic contact, releasing autoinhibition and raising basal kinase activity.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E2", "E4", "E6", "E21", "E8", "E10"], "would_refute": "In predicted or experimental p110\u03b4\u2013p85 complex models, residue 1021 has no atom within about 5 \u00c5 of p85 or of any other chain, and E1021K leaves the predicted p85 binding interface energy and contact count unchanged relative to wild type.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Gain-of-function with enhanced kinase activity is consistent with losing an inhibitory contact, and E21 confirms p85 is the normal partner. But no retrieved source places 1021 at the p85 interface (G2), and the apo structures in E18 are not labelled as complexes, so the interface question is open. This ranks second because the membrane mechanism explains the reported phenotype more directly."}
